\begin{abstract}
We develop a rigorous information-theoretic model of the \emph{energetic cost of reasoning},
transplanting Landauer's principle from physical computation to the elementary steps of a
mathematical proof. Modeling each proof step as a function $f : \alpha \to \beta$ between
finite state spaces, we define the \emph{erased information} of a step as the drop in
Shannon capacity between its input and output registers,
$\erased(f) = \log_2 |\alpha| - \log_2 \imcard(f)$, and the associated \emph{Landauer cost}
as $\erased(f)\cdot k_B T \ln 2$. Within this model we prove: (i) erasure is nonnegative;
(ii) a step erases zero bits if and only if it is injective (logically reversible); (iii)
Landauer's principle in strict form; (iv) a data-processing inequality, with erasure
monotone and sub-additive but not additive; (v) Bennett's reversible embedding, whereby
retaining the input renders any step free; (vi) an exponential erasure separation; and
(vii) an incompressibility bound of Kolmogorov type, so that some Boolean predicate on $n$
bits admits no description shorter than $n$ bits and its verification dissipates at least
$n\,k_B T \ln 2$.
\end{abstract}

\section{Introduction}

Landauer's principle (Landauer, 1961) asserts that the erasure of one bit of information in
a physical system coupled to a thermal reservoir at absolute temperature $T$ must dissipate
at least $k_B T \ln 2$ of energy as heat, where $k_B$ is Boltzmann's constant. It draws a
sharp line between \emph{logically reversible} operations, which map inputs bijectively to
outputs and can in principle be performed at zero cost, and \emph{logically irreversible}
operations, which merge distinct inputs and thereby destroy information. Bennett (1973,
1982) showed that any computation can be made reversible by retaining intermediate results,
so that the thermodynamic cost of computation is attributable entirely to erasure.

This paper asks whether the same accounting applies to \emph{mathematical reasoning}. We
regard a proof as a finite sequence of elementary steps---rewrites, substitutions, case
merges, lookups, and the terminal verification of a claim---each of which transforms a
finite space of reasoning states into another. Some steps are reversible (they lose no
information); others collapse many possibilities into few, and it is these that carry a
thermodynamic cost. Our aim is to make this analogy precise, prove the fundamental
structural results, and exhibit theorems whose verification is provably expensive.

\section{The model}

Throughout, $\alpha$ and $\beta$ denote nonempty finite sets, and $|\alpha|$ denotes the
cardinality of $\alpha$. A \emph{proof step} is any function $f : \alpha \to \beta$. We
think of $\alpha$ as the register of possible states before the step and $\beta$ as the
register after.

\begin{definition}[Image count]
The \emph{image count} of a step $f : \alpha \to \beta$ is the number of distinct outputs
it produces, $\imcard(f) = |\{\, f(x) : x \in \alpha \,\}|$.
\end{definition}

We record three elementary facts: $\imcard(f) \le |\alpha|$; when $\beta$ is finite,
$\imcard(f) \le |\beta|$; and when $\alpha$ is nonempty, $\imcard(f) \ge 1$. Moreover $f$
is injective if and only if $\imcard(f) = |\alpha|$.

\section{Erased information and the reversibility criterion}

\begin{definition}[Erased bits]
The \emph{erased information} of a step $f : \alpha \to \beta$ is
\[
  \erased(f) \;=\; \log_2 |\alpha| \;-\; \log_2 \imcard(f).
\]
Both terms are the Shannon capacities (in bits) of the respective registers under the
uniform distribution; their difference is the information rendered irrecoverable by $f$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Nonnegativity]
For every step $f$ on a nonempty domain, $\erased(f) \ge 0$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Since $1 \le \imcard(f) \le |\alpha|$ and $\log_2$ is monotone increasing on the positive
reals, $\log_2 \imcard(f) \le \log_2 |\alpha|$, so the difference is nonnegative.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Reversibility criterion]
For a step $f$ on a nonempty finite domain, $\erased(f) = 0$ if and only if $f$ is
injective.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
If $f$ is injective then $\imcard(f) = |\alpha|$, so both logarithms coincide and the
erasure is zero. Conversely, if the erasure is zero then $\log_2|\alpha| = \log_2
\imcard(f)$; since $\log_2$ is injective on the positive reals, $|\alpha| = \imcard(f)$, and
a function on a finite set whose image has the same cardinality as its domain is injective.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Bijections are free]
If $f$ is a bijection then $\erased(f) = 0$.
\end{corollary}

A non-identity step may still be free: the Boolean NOT gate $b \mapsto \lnot b$ is a
bijection distinct from the identity, hence erases zero bits. Activity is not cost; only
irreversibility is.

\section{The Landauer cost}

\begin{definition}[Landauer cost]
For a nonnegative quantity of erased bits $b$, Boltzmann constant $k_B$, and temperature
$T$, the \emph{Landauer cost} is $\cost(b, k_B, T) = b \cdot k_B\, T \ln 2$. The cost of a
step $f$ is $\cost(\erased(f), k_B, T)$.
\end{definition}

When $b, k_B, T \ge 0$ the cost is nonnegative, since $\ln 2 > 0$.

\begin{theorem}[Landauer's principle, strict form]
If $f$ is not injective and $k_B, T > 0$, then $\cost(\erased(f), k_B, T) > 0$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
By the reversibility criterion, $f$ non-injective gives $\erased(f) \ne 0$, and by
nonnegativity $\erased(f) > 0$. Since $k_B, T > 0$ and $\ln 2 > 0$, the product is strictly
positive.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Landauer lower bound]
If $f : \alpha \to \beta$ has output in a finite register $\beta$, then
$\erased(f) \ge \log_2 |\alpha| - \log_2 |\beta|$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Since $\imcard(f) \le |\beta|$ and $\log_2$ is monotone, $\log_2 \imcard(f) \le \log_2
|\beta|$; substituting into the definition of erasure gives the bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{example}[The AND gate]
The Boolean conjunction $\land : \{F,T\}^2 \to \{F,T\}$ maps its four inputs to two outputs
(three to $F$, one to $T$), so $\imcard(\land) = 2$ and
$\erased(\land) = \log_2 4 - \log_2 2 = 1$ bit---the canonical $k_B T \ln 2$ of Landauer
dissipation.
\end{example}

\section{Data processing: erasure accumulates and is sub-additive}

\begin{lemma}
For steps $f : \alpha \to \beta$ and $g : \beta \to \gamma$,
$\imcard(g \circ f) \le \imcard(f)$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The image of $g \circ f$ is the image under $g$ of the image of $f$, and applying a function
cannot increase cardinality.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Data-processing inequality]
For composable steps $f$ and $g$, $\erased(f) \le \erased(g \circ f)$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
By the preceding lemma, $\imcard(g\circ f) \le \imcard(f)$; monotonicity of $\log_2$ gives
$\log_2 \imcard(g\circ f) \le \log_2 \imcard(f)$. Since the composite and $f$ share the
domain $\alpha$, subtracting from $\log_2|\alpha|$ yields the inequality.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Non-additivity]
Erasure is not additive under composition: there exist steps $f, g$ with
$\erased(g \circ f) \ne \erased(f) + \erased(g)$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Take $f = g$ to be the constant map on a two-element set, each erasing $1$ bit. Their
composite is again the same constant map, erasing $1$ bit, not $2$.
\end{proof}

Combining the last two results, erasure is sub-additive and monotone but not additive.

\section{Bennett's reversible embedding}

\begin{definition}[Reversible embedding]
For a step $f : \alpha \to \beta$, its \emph{Bennett embedding} is
$\tilde f : \alpha \to \alpha \times \beta$, $\tilde f(x) = (x, f(x))$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}
$\tilde f$ is injective.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
If $\tilde f(a) = \tilde f(b)$ then their first coordinates agree, so $a = b$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Reversible computation is free]
For any step $f$, $\erased(\tilde f) = 0$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
$\tilde f$ is injective, so by the reversibility criterion its erasure vanishes.
\end{proof}

The embedding keeps a copy of the input alongside the output; hence no computation
intrinsically requires erasure. The Landauer cost of a proof is a cost of \emph{forgetting},
incurred only when scratch work is discarded.

\section{Explicit erasure families and the exponential separation}

\begin{definition}[Collapse families]
For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the \emph{linear collapse} $C_n$ maps a $2^n$-state search space
onto a single answer. For $m \in \mathbb{N}$, the \emph{big collapse} $B_m$ maps a
$2^{(2^m)}$-state space onto a single answer.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Erasure of a collapse]
A constant step on a nonempty domain $\gamma$ erases $\log_2 |\gamma|$ bits. Consequently
$\erased(C_n) = n$ and $\erased(B_m) = 2^m$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
A constant map has image count $1$, so its erasure is $\log_2 |\gamma| - \log_2 1 = \log_2
|\gamma|$. For $C_n$, $|\gamma| = 2^n$ gives $n$; for $B_m$, $|\gamma| = 2^{(2^m)}$ gives
$2^m$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Exponential relation]
$\erased(B_m) = 2^{\,\erased(C_m)}$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
$\erased(B_m) = 2^m = 2^{\,\erased(C_m)}$ by the previous theorem.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Exponential erasure separation]
For every real bound $C$ there exists $m$ with $\erased(B_m) > C$. Hence there are
verifications whose erasure---and therefore Landauer heat at any fixed positive
temperature---is unbounded, growing exponentially in the size parameter.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Since $2^m \to \infty$, choose $m$ with $2^m > C$; then $\erased(B_m) = 2^m > C$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Exponential heat]
The dissipated heat of the big collapse is
$\cost(\erased(B_m), k_B, T) = 2^m \cdot k_B T \ln 2$, exponential in $m$.
\end{corollary}

\section{Incompressibility and the cost of verification}

\begin{theorem}[Incompressibility]
For every $n$, there is no injective map from the set of Boolean predicates on $n$ bits to
the set of programs of length strictly less than $n$ bits.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
The register of interest has $2^n$ elements---the $2^n$ Boolean-valued cells of a truth
table on $n$ bits. The number of programs of length strictly less than $n$ is
$2^0 + 2^1 + \dots + 2^{n-1} = 2^n - 1$. An injection from a set of size $2^n$ into a set of
size $2^n - 1$ is impossible by the pigeonhole principle.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Thermodynamic cost of verification]
For each $n$ there is a predicate whose shortest description has length at least $n$ bits.
Storing and subsequently erasing its description erases at least $n$ bits and therefore
dissipates at least $n \cdot k_B\, T \ln 2$ of heat at temperature $T$.
\end{corollary}

This is the qualitative shadow of Kolmogorov complexity: incompressible objects abound, and
their verification is irreducibly costly.

\section{Applications and future work}

\paragraph{Reversible computing.} Since erasure, not computation, is the sole source of
cost, a machine that never discards information can in principle operate arbitrarily close
to zero energy per operation---the theoretical basis of adiabatic and reversible logic.

\paragraph{Complexity theory.} The exponential separation and incompressibility floor
attach a physical quantity---dissipated heat---to the intuition that some theorems are
harder than others, suggesting a thermodynamic reading of proof complexity.

\paragraph{Open directions.} (1) A creation/erasure ledger with an explicit creation
primitive and a cost functional over full proofs, conjecturally obeying
$\mathrm{create} + \mathrm{erase} \ge K(\text{predicate})$. (2) Genuine Kolmogorov
complexity $K$ relative to a universal machine, with a verification bound of $K(x) - O(1)$
erased bits. (3) A concrete decision problem whose answer is short but whose cheapest

/-- **Bennett's reversible embedding** of a step `f`: keep the input alongside the output,
`x ↦ (x, f x)`. -/
def bennettEmbedding {α β : Type*} (f : α → β) : α → α × β := fun x => (x, f x)

lemma bennettEmbedding_injective {α β : Type*} (f : α → β) :
    Function.Injective (bennettEmbedding f) := by
  intro a b h; exact (Prod.mk.injEq _ _ _ _ ▸ h).1

irreversibility — not computation itself — is what carries the Landauer cost. -/
theorem erasedBits_bennett {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β] [Nonempty α]
    (f : α → β) : erasedBits (bennettEmbedding f) = 0 :=
  (erasedBits_eq_zero_iff_injective _).2 (bennettEmbedding_injective f)

    imageCard (fun _ : γ => c) = 1 := by
  unfold imageCard; rw [Finset.image_const Finset.univ_nonempty]; simp

lemma erasedBits_const {γ δ : Type*} [Fintype γ] [DecidableEq δ] [Nonempty γ] (c : δ) :
    erasedBits (fun _ : γ => c) = Real.logb 2 (Fintype.card γ) := by
  unfold erasedBits; rw [imageCard_const]; simp

bits. -/
noncomputable def collapse (n : ℕ) : Fin (2^n) → Fin 1 := fun _ => 0

lemma erasedBits_collapse (n : ℕ) : erasedBits (collapse n) = n := by
  unfold erasedBits collapse
  rw [imageCard_const (0 : Fin 1)]
  simp [Fintype.card_fin, Real.logb_pow, Real.logb_self_eq_one]

/-- A doubly-exponential state space collapsed to one answer: erases `2ᵐ` bits. -/
noncomputable def bigCollapse (m : ℕ) : Fin (2^(2^m)) → Fin 1 := fun _ => 0

lemma erasedBits_bigCollapse (m : ℕ) : erasedBits (bigCollapse m) = 2 ^ m := by
  unfold erasedBits bigCollapse
  rw [imageCard_const (0 : Fin 1)]
  simp [Fintype.card_fin, Real.logb_pow, Real.logb_self_eq_one]

/-- The exponential family erases `2` raised to the erasure of the linear family: the erasure
of `bigCollapse m` is exponential in the erasure of `collapse m`. -/
theorem erasedBits_bigCollapse_exp (m : ℕ) :
    erasedBits (bigCollapse m) = Real.rpow 2 (erasedBits (collapse m)) := by
  rw [erasedBits_bigCollapse, erasedBits_collapse]; exact (Real.rpow_natCast 2 m).symm

lemma two_pow_unbounded (C : ℝ) : ∃ m : ℕ, C < (2:ℝ) ^ m := by
  obtain ⟨m, hm⟩ := pow_unbounded_of_one_lt (max C 0) (by norm_num : (1:ℝ) < 2)
  exact ⟨m, lt_of_le_of_lt (le_max_left _ _) hm⟩

/-- **Exponential erasure separation.** There exist theorems (state collapses) whose
verification erases arbitrarily — indeed exponentially — many bits, hence dissipates
arbitrarily much Landauer heat at fixed positive temperature. -/
theorem exponential_erasure_separation (C : ℝ) :
    ∃ m : ℕ, C < erasedBits (bigCollapse m) := by
  obtain ⟨m, hm⟩ := two_pow_unbounded C
  exact ⟨m, by rw [erasedBits_bigCollapse]; exact hm⟩

/-- Physical restatement: the dissipated heat of collapsing `bigCollapse m` is
`2ᵐ · kB · T · ln 2`, exponential in `m`. -/
theorem landauerCost_bigCollapse (m : ℕ) (kB T : ℝ) :
    landauerCost (erasedBits (bigCollapse m)) kB T = (2:ℝ) ^ m * (kB * T * Real.log 2) := by
  rw [erasedBits_bigCollapse]; rfl

/-! ## Kolmogorov incompressibility and the cost of verification -/

/-- **Incompressibility (Kolmogorov counting bound).** There is no injective code sending the
`2ⁿ` Boolean predicates on `n` bits to the `2ⁿ − 1` programs of length `< n`.  Consequently
some predicate has no description (proof) shorter than `n` bits; storing/erasing its truth
table costs `≥ n · kB T ln 2` by Landauer's principle. -/
theorem incompressible (n : ℕ) :
    ¬ ∃ D : (Fin n → Bool) → Fin (2^n - 1), Function.Injective D := by
  rintro ⟨D, hD⟩
  have hcard : Fintype.card (Fin n → Bool) ≤ Fintype.card (Fin (2^n - 1)) :=
    Fintype.card_le_of_injective D hD
  simp only [Fintype.card_fun, Fintype.card_bool, Fintype.card_fin] at hcard
  have h2 : 0 < 2^n := Nat.two_pow_pos n
  omega

end ThermoProof
